The Challenge

Creative reviews need more than a personal preference

The objective: bring consistency and objectivity to ad evaluations, using AI to examine colour, copy and call-to-action through a repeatable set of questions.

Different opinions

A visual can trigger many reactions. The team needs a shared way to explain what works and what needs attention.

Unclear messages

Strong design can still leave the audience unsure about the main message or the benefit being communicated.

Missing next steps

A memorable headline needs a clear action. Reviewers should be able to identify what the audience can do next.

Inconsistent reviews

Feedback scattered across conversations makes it harder to compare iterations and retain the reasoning behind a change.

HMC Approach

Give every creative the same thoughtful questions.

Turn an uploaded visual into a structured first review, then give the marketing team the context to refine it.

The Solution

Upload a creative. Get a more useful conversation.

An AI-powered internal tool lets teams upload ad visuals and receive structured insights on design tone, message clarity, CTA effectiveness and brand alignment.

A focused creative brief

Three changes. A clearer handoff.

  1. 01
    Lead with one message

    Use a concise headline and one supporting line instead of several competing ideas.

  2. 02
    Make the action explicit

    Give the CTA a visible label and connect it to a defined next step.

  3. 03
    Strengthen the hierarchy

    Use contrast and space to separate brand, message and action.

Scores are hand-authored examples of this rubric. The concepts have not been tested with customers.

Faster reviews. More evidence in the discussion.
The tool enabled faster, insight-driven creative reviews, helping the marketing team refine campaigns with evidence-based feedback rather than subjective opinion.
A shared structure for a better first review.

Sources & methodology
Know what each part represents
The case study and source images
The objective, solution and qualitative outcome come from the supplied case brief. Two screenshots are embedded as supplied. The screenshots document the original Gemini-based tool; the optional live analyzer on this page has been adapted to OpenAI. The analysis screenshot is cropped at the CTA section. Any offer text inside the historical screenshot is part of that reference, not a current offer reproduced by this page. No measured time saving, lead uplift or conversion change was supplied.
Demonstration concepts and scores
The initial and refined concepts are newly constructed examples. Their observations and 0–5 scores are hand-authored to demonstrate a repeatable review structure. They are not a transcription of the original tool’s output and were not generated by a live API call. The weighted index is 100 × Σ(score × weight) ÷ [5 × Σ(weight)] only when all four dimensions are assessed and total weight is greater than zero. If any dimension is unassessed, the index is withheld and coverage is shown. All-zero weights also make the index unavailable. A higher index means a higher assessment under this illustrative rubric, not better campaign performance.
Local image colour analysis
Images are decoded in the browser and sampled on a small canvas. Transparency is composited over white. RGB values are grouped into colour buckets; the six largest buckets and a remainder category describe approximate pixel shares. Palette extraction does not infer message meaning, audience response or brand compliance. Local uploads stay in the tab unless you explicitly run the OpenAI option.
Live OpenAI review
The optional integration sends the selected image and brief to the OpenAI Responses API using your entered API key, only after you choose Analyze with OpenAI. It requests structured JSON observations for colour, copy, CTA and brand cues. Unreadable or insufficient evidence should yield an unscored dimension. AI output can be incomplete or mistaken; check the source creative. The key is held only in the page’s memory and excluded from downloads. A shared production implementation should route requests through a server that keeps its credentials private.
Contrast calculation
The checker uses sRGB relative luminance and (lighter luminance + 0.05) ÷ (darker luminance + 0.05). The displayed WCAG AA reference points are 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. Large text is generally at least 18 pt regular or 14 pt bold. This is a colour-pair check, not a whole-ad accessibility certification. See W3C’s contrast guidance.
3D scene, comparison and workflow
The 3D composition separates conceptual creative layers; it does not simulate eye tracking. The divider compares two illustrative visuals. API workflow playback is a labelled simulation; live requests use the dedicated OpenAI control. D3 and Three.js are embedded with their licences, with Canvas rendering available when WebGL is unavailable.
